title: Personal Checking: The Claim Amount and the Disputed Debit as Limits on a Provisional Credit
content:
## Rule

On a Personal Checking account where a single electronic-transaction dispute is in submitted status, the provisional credit on that dispute is held within two limits taken from the records:

- **The claim amount** — the sum the owner asserts is in error, as recorded on the dispute;
- **The debit amount** — the full amount of the disputed debit entry.

The credit can never exceed either of them. Taken together, these two limits allow no more than the lower of the claim amount and the debit amount; when the claim amount is larger than the debit, the debit amount is the one that binds.

## Condition, judgement, figure

| Claim amount compared with debit amount | Figure these limits allow |
|---|---|
| claim below the debit | the claim amount |
| claim equal to the debit | that shared amount |
| claim above the debit | the debit amount |

## Hypothetical examples

- The owner claims 40.00 USD on a 60.00 USD debit: these limits allow 40.00 USD.
- The owner claims 80.00 USD on a 60.00 USD debit: these limits allow 60.00 USD, since a credit can never exceed the debit disputed.
- A duplicate-charge claim for the full 23.19 USD of a 23.19 USD debit: 23.19 USD.

Both figures carry two decimal places, so choosing between them involves no rounding.
